name: Bozeman
summary: A booming college town in the mountains with one of the great dinosaur museums in the world and hot springs all around — the northern gateway to Yellowstone.

foodMustTry.name: Farm-to-table & craft beer
foodMustTry.blurb: Bozeman's food scene has taken off.

item.title: Museum of the Rockies
item.blurb: One of the world's great dinosaur collections — the T. rex and Triceratops of Montana's badlands.

item.title: Main Street & a hot spring
item.blurb: Historic Main Street, then a soak at a nearby hot spring.

days.label: Day 536 — Big Sky, then Yellowstone
days.summary: Down US-191 past Lone Peak to the west gate.

drive.scenicNote: South on US-191 into the Gallatin Canyon, with the river on your right the whole way — they filmed A River Runs Through It along here.

item.title: The Lone Peak Tram at Big Sky

location.name: Big Sky Resort
location.address: 50 Big Sky Resort Rd, Big Sky, MT

item.blurb: Big Sky is the largest ski resort in the United States — nearly six thousand acres — and the tram hauls you to the 11,166-ft summit of Lone Peak, a rock fin standing alone above everything. Three states from the top on a clear day, and the Yellowstone plateau laid out to the south. The runs off this summit are the serious kind; in summer it is simply the best view in Montana that you can reach without walking.

drive.scenicNote: The rest of the canyon to West Yellowstone and in through the west gate.
